pages.summary: The filters of a discrete wavelet: lowpass and highpass, for decomposition and reconstruction.
body: `wfilters` gives the four filters of a wavelet by name: `'haar'`, `'db1'` to `'db45'` (Daubechies), `'sym2'` to `'sym20'` (symlets, nearly symmetric), `'coif1'` to `'coif5'` (coiflets, with vanishing moments of the scaling function too), and the biorthogonal `'bior'` and `'rbio'` families. For an orthogonal wavelet the reconstruction lowpass filter LoR sums to sqrt(2) and has norm 1, LoD is LoR reversed, and the highpass filters alternate their signs. `dbwavf`, `symwavf` and `coifwavf` give the scaling filter LoR/sqrt(2), which sums to 1.

examples.title: The four filters of db2
examples.code:
[LoD, HiD, LoR, HiR] = wfilters('db2');
LoR
[sum(LoR), norm(LoR)]
isequal(LoD, fliplr(LoR))
F = dbwavf('db2');
max(abs(F*sqrt(2) - LoR)) < 1e-15
numel(symwavf('sym4'))
subplot(2, 2, 1), stem(LoD), title('LoD')
subplot(2, 2, 2), stem(HiD), title('HiD')
subplot(2, 2, 3), stem(LoR), title('LoR')
subplot(2, 2, 4), stem(HiR), title('HiR')

pages.summary: Filters made from a scaling filter: the mirror filter, and the four filters of an orthogonal or biorthogonal wavelet.
body: `qmf` reverses a filter and changes the sign of every other coefficient: the highpass filter that goes with a lowpass one. `orthfilt` makes the four filters of an orthogonal wavelet from its scaling filter (scaled to norm 1). `biorfilt` makes them from a biorthogonal pair, the decomposition and reconstruction scaling filters, each scaled to sum sqrt(2) and padded to one even length.

examples.title: db3 from its scaling filter, and the bior2.2 pair

pages.summary: How the discrete transforms extend a signal past its ends, and how deep a decomposition can usefully go.
body: A filter at the ends of a signal reaches past them, and the extension mode says what it finds there: `'sym'` (the signal mirrored, the default), `'symw'`, `'asym'`, `'asymw'`, `'zpd'` (zeros), `'sp0'`, `'sp1'`, `'ppd'` (periodic) or `'per'` (periodization, which gives exactly half as many coefficients). The mode holds for every discrete transform until changed; each also takes `'mode', m` for one call. `wmaxlev` gives the deepest level at which some coefficient is still free of the extension.

pages.summary: One level of the discrete wavelet transform, and its inverse.
body: `dwt` filters a signal by the decomposition lowpass and highpass filters and keeps every second sample: the approximation coefficients cA (the slow part) and the detail coefficients cD (the fast part), each about half as long. `idwt` puts the signal back from them: upsampled, filtered by the reconstruction filters and added. Either input may be [] for zeros.
syntax: The middle L samples of the inverse.
With an extension mode for this call.

examples.title: A ramp by Haar, and back by db2

pages.summary: A multilevel decomposition: dwt repeated on the approximations, and the signal back from it.
body: `wavedec` applies `dwt` n times, each time to the approximation the last one left, and packs the coefficients into one vector c = [cA_n, cD_n, ..., cD_1] with their lengths in l (the signal's length last). `waverec` reverses it exactly. `appcoef` gives the approximation coefficients at a level, `detcoef` the details of one level or several.

examples.title: A tone with a step, to level 4

pages.summary: The parts of a signal from one level of its decomposition, and the energy in each.
body: `wrcoef` reconstructs the signal from one kind of coefficient alone, the others set to zero: `'a'` the approximation at level n, `'d'` the details of level n. The approximation at level n and the details of levels 1 to n add up to the signal. `upcoef` reconstructs a vector of coefficients straight up n levels. `wenergy` gives the percentage of the coefficients' energy in the approximation and in the details of each level.
syntax: X = wrcoef('a', c, l, wname, n)
X = wrcoef('d', c, l, wname, n)

examples.title: The parts add up to the signal

pages.summary: One level of the discrete wavelet transform of an image, and its inverse.
body: `dwt2` applies `dwt` along the rows and then down the columns: the approximation cA (lowpass both ways), the horizontal details cH (highpass down the columns, so horizontal edges), the vertical details cV and the diagonal ones cD, each about a quarter of the image. `idwt2` puts the image back; any of the four may be [] for zeros.
syntax: [cA, cH, cV, cD] = dwt2(X, LoD, HiD)
X = idwt2(cA, cH, cV, cD, wname)
X = idwt2(cA, cH, cV, cD, wname, S)

examples.title: A disc and a step, by Haar

pages.summary: A multilevel decomposition of an image, and the image back from it or from one part.
body: `wavedec2` applies `dwt2` n times to the approximations and packs every coefficient into one row C, with the sizes in S (the approximation's first, then each level's details from the deepest, then the image's). `waverec2` reverses it. `appcoef2` gives the approximation at a level, `detcoef2` the horizontal, vertical or diagonal details (`'all'` gives the three), and `wrcoef2` the image reconstructed from one kind of coefficient at a level.
syntax: [H, V, D] = detcoef2('all', C, S, n)
X = wrcoef2(type, C, S, wname, n)

examples.title: Two levels of db2

pages.summary: The stationary wavelet transform: no samples dropped, so that a shift of the signal only shifts its coefficients.
body: `swt` filters by the wavelet's filters with 2^(k-1) - 1 zeros between their taps at level k, periodically and without keeping every second sample: each level's approximations and details are as long as the signal (whose length must be a multiple of 2^n). The transform is redundant but shift-invariant, which suits denoising and finding where things happen. `iswt` inverts it; `swt2` and `iswt2` do the same for images, a page for each level.
syntax: [A, H, V, D] = swt2(X, n, wname)
X = iswt2(A, H, V, D, wname)

examples.title: A tone with a pulse, three levels
An image

pages.summary: The maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform, and the multiresolution analysis it gives.
body: `modwt` gives the wavelet coefficients W_1 to W_J and the scaling coefficients V_J of a signal of any length, each as long as the signal: like the stationary transform, shift-invariant, and its coefficients keep the signal's energy (the sum of their squares is that of the signal). `imodwt` inverts it. `modwtmra` splits the signal into details D_1 to D_J and a smooth S_J, each as long as the signal and lined up with it in time, which add up to the signal. The wavelet is `'sym4'` by default.
syntax: The details and the smooth, a row each.
The signal mirrored at its end first.
